10.1002_adfm.79100: Surface passivation is essential for high‐performance perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, passivator‐induced carrier accumulation in potential wells and the reduction of ion migration activation energy caused by heterointerface energy changes pose significant challenges to device stability. Herein, we demonstrate a nondestructive halide exchange strategy with IBr‐treatment to pre‐construct a positive work function change without incorporating exogenous impurities. By simply varying concentration, this strategy enables continuous adjustment of the heterointerface energetics to suit various perovskites and passivators. The pre‐constructed positive work function change avoids the generation of the potential well during perovskite surface passivation, preventing the electron accumulation and facilitating interfacial hole extraction. Upon the IBr‐treatment, the PSCs achieve outstanding power conversion efficiency of 24.70% with PEAI passivation, 26.19% for small‐area device and 24.48% for 1‐cm 2 device with CHEAI passivation. The devices retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 1500 h continuous light illumination under maximum power point tracking. Our study provides a promising and practical strategy to overcome the passivator‐induced heterointerface energetics changes, avoiding the deteriorated efficiency and stability for the iodine‐containing perovskite photovoltaics.
10.1002_aenm.70964: Anode‐free lithium metal batteries offer a practical route to achieve ultra‐high energy density, yet their implementation is hindered by poor cycling stability and coulombic efficiency resulting from lithiophobic interfaces and nonuniform lithium deposition. To address these challenges, we design a lithium host material by incorporating gallium‐based liquid metal nanodroplets into a 3D porous carbon framework (CF@GaInSn@C). This architecture effectively accommodates electrode volume changes and enables highly stable lithium plating/stripping behavior. The liquid metal nanodroplets function as an atomic composite core, providing abundant lithiophilic sites with low diffusion barriers that promote uniform lithium nucleation and lateral mass transport. This mechanism facilitates dense and homogeneous lithium deposition across the internal pores of the CF@GaInSn@C host. As a result, it demonstrates exceptional reversibility in half cells with a lithium electrode, maintaining a coulombic efficiency of 99.83% over 1500 cycles at 2 mA cm − 2 and 2 mAh cm − 2 . Furthermore, anode‐free full cells coupled with LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 cathodes deliver an average coulombic efficiency of 99.48% after 100 cycles at 0.5 C. This work demonstrates a promising structural design strategy based on liquid metal nanodroplets for regulating lithium deposition, highlighting their significant potential for application in high‐performance anode‐free lithium batteries.
10.1021_acsami.5c24183: High Resolution Image Download MS PowerPoint Slide Achieving high-efficiency perovskite solar cells (PSCs) typically necessitates postdeposition annealing under stringent environmental controls, such as low relative humidity or inert atmospheres. These demanding conditions significantly increase the complexity and cost of device fabrication. Therefore, developing an annealing strategy for obtaining high-quality, phase-pure α-FAPbI 3 perovskite in ambient or high-humidity environments is critically important. Here, we demonstrate that coevaporated FAPbI 3 perovskite active layers annealed in a saturated-humid environment exhibit pure α-phase and thus markedly superior device performance compared to those annealed in normal air or an inert atmosphere. The resulting preferred crystal orientation, superior carrier transport properties, and retarded charge carrier recombination collectively enable an excellent power conversion efficiency (PCE) of up to 21.3% in vacuum-deposited inverted PSCs. Additionally, these devices also deliver excellent performance under indoor environmental light-harvesting, achieving PCEs of 34.9% and 36.7% under 1000 lx illumination from 6500 K and 3000 K fluorescent light sources, respectively.
10.1039_d5ta07989f: TU-82, a 3D [8 + 2]-connected bcu COF, was post-synthetically metalated to yield TU-82-M ( M = Fe, Cu). TU-82-Fe shows outstanding activity and selectivity for electrocatalytic nitrate (NO 3 − ) reduction to ammonia via atomically dispersed Fe sites.
10.1109_tte.2026.3664915: This paper introduces a novel sizing algorithm for an Auxiliary Energy Storage System (AESS) that operates within non-dissipative equalization topologies utilizing bidirectional DC/DC converters, developed for battery powered motor drive applications. The sizing algorithm integrates both equalization and dynamic energy support functions to determine the optimal AESS energy capacity and power specifications. The key objectives of the proposed sizing methodology are to fulfil the desired equalization and dynamic support of the main battery with the minimum cost, mass, and volume by also considering the ageing process of both the main battery and the AESS. This can be accomplished by considering the specific energy and operating demands of the application, the characteristics of the candidate storage technologies that may be used for AESS (such as Li-ion batteries or supercapacitors), and the system longevity. Thus, aging models are integrated to consider AESS degradation for ensuring its viability for second-life use and thus, maximizing asset value. A significant advantage of the proposed AESS sizing methodology is its broad applicability, as it is both model- and hardware-agnostic. The algorithm's effectiveness is validated through both simulation and experimental results on a cell-to-cell equalization topology, and several results are presented to demonstrate the operating improvements.
